outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Background for Parameter-Efficient Finetuning
outline.description: Introduces the need for efficient adaptation of large foundation models, reviews existing finetuning paradigms, and sets the stage for orthogonal finetuning.
subtopics: Scaling of foundation models and the finetuning problem
Overview of model finetuning, adapter tuning, and prompt tuning
Limitations of full finetuning and parameter‑efficient alternatives
Key concepts: parameter efficiency, inference latency, and knowledge preservation

outline.description: Explains the orthogonal finetuning framework, its mathematical formulation, and why its parameter count can be prohibitive.
subtopics: Geometric motivation: preserving pairwise neuron angles
Formal definition of OFT: multiplicative orthogonal update
Cayley parameterization of orthogonal matrices
Block‑diagonal OFT: sparsity vs. expressivity trade‑off
Analysis of parameter count and inductive biases in block‑diagonal OFT

outline.chapter_title: Information Transmission Perspective on Orthogonal Matrices
outline.description: Reframes the construction of dense orthogonal transforms as an information transmission problem on a grid graph, providing intuition for sparse factorization.
subtopics: Dense connectivity as a graph problem
Factorizing a matrix into a product of sparse matrices
Directed edges, levels, and path‑based dense connectivity
Desiderata: dense connectivity and minimal free edges
ω‑edge counting under orthogonality constraints

outline.description: Introduces butterfly matrices, their origin in the FFT, and how they provide efficient sparse factorizations with ϴ(d log d) parameters.
subtopics: Cooley‑Tukey FFT and butterfly graphs
Definition of butterfly factors and recursive butterfly matrices
Block‑butterfly components and permutation structure
Ensuring orthogonality of each component (Cayley or 2×2 rotations)
Parameter count analysis: O(d log d) vs. O(d^2) and O(bd)

outline.description: Details how butterfly factorization is integrated into OFT to create BOFT, including initialization, dropout, and forward‑pass equations.
subtopics: Full BOFT formulation: R(m,b)=∏_{i=1}^m \tilde{B}^b_{(d,i)}
Special cases: reduction to block‑diagonal OFT and full OFT
(m,b) hyper‑parameters and their effect on expressivity/efficiency
Identity initialization via zero skew‑symmetric matrices
Multiplicative dropout scheme for BOFT
